thread:
Alice Kim: Heads up — starting ~01:10 UTC we saw a large spike in prefix cache misses. Backend CPU + fetch rate jumped, and p99 token latency climbed. Cache hit-rate fell from ~92% -> ~12% over a ~3m window. Investigating now.

Raj Patel: Can you paste some sample keys so we can see the churn?

Alice Kim: Pasting a few anonymized samples we collected from the hot shard: 
```
prompt_key:model:v1:customer:acme:lang:en-US:prefix:"Tell me a joke"
prompt_key:model:v1:customer:acme:lang:en-US:prefix:"Tell me a joke "
prompt_key:model:v1:customer:acme:lang:en:prefix:"Tell me a joke"
```
Seeing the same base text with tiny variants (trailing space, lang tag differences). Also spotted differing tokenization outputs after the 1769 tokenizer rollout — same user produced two different token sequences.

Mateo Rivera: Is that the tokenizer PR I merged this morning? I added an optional normalization flag but default was off for prewarmers.

Emily Zhao: SRE: can we throttle origin fetches to stop a stampede on the backend while you investigate? Suggest a token-bucket per-origin-key fetch limit.

oncall-sre: Applying emergency rate-limit on cache origin for affected shards now — 10 req/s per shard. Monitoring CPU and fetch queues.

infra-bot: deploybot: Updated config r10 -> cache_origin_rate_limit=10/s. Deployed to prod in 28s. :white_check_mark:

Raj Patel: Nice, we should also add jitter to prewarmers and any warmup cron so they don't all fetch the same key simultaneously. Example: 
```
sleep_ms = base_ms + rand(0, jitter_ms)
```
and exponential backoff on repeated misses.

Alice Kim: After the rate-limit, backend CPU dropped from ~92% -> ~45% within ~2m, p99 latency improved. Good emergency mitigation, but we need a real fix.

Mateo Rivera: Root cause looks like a key-normalization mismatch between runtime and pre-warm worker. Runtime used post-tokenizer normalized form; pre-warm used raw text. That explains the high cardinality and duplicated keys. Working on a patch to canonicalize keys to collapsed-whitespace + lowercase + token-based checksum.

Emily Zhao: For rollback/disable: we have a feature flag cache.prewarm.enabled — could selectively disable prewarm for customers with high unique prefix counts. Did we already toggle anything?

Alice Kim: We toggled prewarm off for customers with >100k active prefixes to reduce load while patch is prepared.

Raj Patel: Long-term proposal:
- Canonicalize keys at ingress (normalize unicode, collapse whitespace, lowercase, token-based hash)
- Per-customer cache quotas and eviction bias for noisy customers
- Route high-miss flows to a cheaper/fast-fallback model variant instead of origin fetches
- Add alerting: trigger when hit-rate drops >15% and backend CPU >60% for >2m

Mateo Rivera: I'll open the PR for canonicalization + unit tests. Also propose using a fixed-length checksum of the normalized token list instead of full text in key to avoid key length explosion.

oncall-sre: Can you also add origin-side rate-limits and a small negative-caching TTL for repeated misses? That would help reduce repeated origin pressure on bad keys.

Mateo Rivera: Good call. We'll implement a short negative TTL (30s) for keys that miss more than N times in M seconds.

Alice Kim: Quick canonicalization example for review: 
```
def canonical_key(text, model, lang):
    s = normalize_unicode(text)
    s = collapse_whitespace(s).lower()
    tokens = tokenize(s, model)
    return f"pk:{model}:{lang}:{hash(tuple(tokens))}"
```

Raj Patel: Also add normalization of headers used in keying (e.g., accept-language fallback to just language code) — header diffs were creating separate keys for en vs en-US.

Emily Zhao: I'll start the postmortem draft. Initial severity: Sev3 (transient latency + increased CPU, partial mitigation applied quickly). Will include timeline, mitigations, and follow-up owners.

Mateo Rivera: PR opened: github.com/redwood/server/pull/5123 — contains canonicalization, tests, and migration steps for existing key namespace. Planning canary tomorrow then global rollout if canary looks good.

Alice Kim: Thanks everyone. Add me to reviews and the postmortem doc. :thumbsup:

Raj Patel: Follow-ups to track: PR review (Mateo), origin negative caching + rate-limits (SRE), per-customer quotas (platform), and alert tuning (observability).

Emily Zhao: Noted — I'll assign owners in the postmortem. Closing the incident thread once the canary is green. :lock:
